action: Set this event in your instance initialization file to enable gathering of statistics for data redaction.
note: This is not a user error number or message. This message does not need to be translated or documented.

description: The input and output lengths of the redaction do not match.
cause: As specified, the redaction parameters produced an output with a length different to that of the input.
action: Use regular expression redaction instead of partial redaction.

description: The data redaction policy expression has an error. %s
cause: The data redaction policy expression had an error.
action: Specify a valid policy expression. Write the data redaction policy expression in SQL, and include a valid predicate to use in the following SQL query: SELECT 1 FROM DUAL WHERE <policy_expression>;

description: The policy expression has an unsupported (use of) operator '%s'.
cause: The policy expression used an unsupported operator, or used an operator in an unsupported way.
action: Modify the policy expression to use only the supported operators in a supported way. Supported operators include "=", "!=", ">", "<", ">=", "<=", the length operators, the substring operators, and the context operators (SYS_CONTEXT and XS_SYS_CONTEXT). For a complete list of the supported operators, and the supported ways the allowed operators can be used, refer to the section on data redaction policy expressions in the Oracle documentation.

description: The policy expression has an unsupported PL/SQL function %s.%s.%s.
cause: The policy expression had an unsupported PL/SQL function.
action: Modify the policy expression to use a supported PL/SQL function. The supported PL/SQL functions include the Oracle Label Security dominates functions, and the Oracle Apex session state functions, V and NV. Refer to Oracle database documentation for additional information.

description: invalid SYS_CONTEXT namespace %s in policy expression
cause: The SYS_CONTEXT (or XS_SYS_CONTEXT) namespace used in the policy expression was not valid.
action: Modify the policy expression to use a valid namespace. Supported namespaces include USERENV, SYS_SESSION_ROLES, XS$SESSION and the namespaces listed in the DBA_CONTEXT catalog view.

description: unsupported nesting of function %s.%s.%s within function %s.%s.%s in policy expression
cause: The policy expression had an unsupported PL/SQL function nesting.
action: Modify the policy expression to use only supported PL/SQL function nesting. The Oracle Label Security functions NUMERIC_LABEL, CHAR_TO_LABEL, and SA_SESSION can only be used from within the Oracle Label Security dominates functions. For a complete list of supported PL/SQL function nesting, refer to the section on writing policy expressions in the Oracle documentation for data redaction.

description: unsupported use of PL/SQL function %s.%s.%s in policy expression
cause: The policy expression used a PL/SQL function in an unsupported way.
action: Modify the policy expression to use the PL/SQL function properly. The parameters to the Oracle Label Security functions NUMERIC_LABEL, CHAR_TO_LABEL, and SA_SESSION must be constants. For a complete list of the supported ways that PL/SQL functions can be used in a policy expression, refer to the Oracle documentation.

description: The parameter %s with value '%s' has an error.
cause: The value of the parameter had an error. If DBMS_REDACT.CREATE_POLICY_EXPRESSION was invoked and the POLICY_EXPRESSION_NAME parameter had an error, the policy expression name either already existed, or was invalid. If DBMS_REDACT.DROP_POLICY_EXPRESSION was invoked and the POLICY_EXPRESSION_NAME parameter had an error, the policy expression either did not exist, was still in use (was applied to a column), or was invalid. If DBMS_REDACT.APPLY_POLICY_EXPR_TO_COL was invoked and the POLICY_EXPRESSION_NAME parameter had an error, a policy expression may already exist on this column. Only one policy expression may be associated with any given column. The name of any Oracle Data Redaction policy expression associated with a given column can be found in the REDACTION_EXPRESSIONS catalog view. If the DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY was invoked and the OBJECT_SCHEMA parameter referenced the APEX, Sharding (GSMADMIN_INTERNAL), or Spatial installation schema, the operation was prevented. Data redaction policies are not supported on objects within the APEX, Sharding (GSMADMIN_INTERNAL), or Spatial installation schema. If the DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY was invoked and the OBJECT_NAME referenced a metadata-linked view, the operation was prevented. Data redaction policies are not supported on metadata-linked views. If the DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY was invoked and the OBJECT_NAME referenced an OLAP analytic workspace table, the operation was prevented. Data redaction policies are not supported on OLAP analytic workspaces.
action: Provide a valid value for the parameter. If DBMS_REDACT.CREATE_POLICY_EXPRESSION was invoked and the parameter was POLICY_EXPRESSION_NAME, provide a valid (new or existing) policy expression name. The names of all existing Oracle Data Redaction policy expressions can be found in the REDACTION_EXPRESSIONS catalog view. For the POLICY_EXPRESSION_NAME parameter of the DBMS_REDACT.DROP_POLICY_EXPRESSION procedure, provide a valid existing policy expression name that is not currently in use (applied to any column). The names of the columns to which a given policy expression is currently applied can be found in the REDACTION_EXPRESSIONS catalog view. For the POLICY_EXPRESSION_NAME parameter of the DBMS_REDACT.APPLY_POLICY_EXPR_TO_COL procedure, either provide NULL to remove the current policy expression association of the column, or provide a valid existing policy expression name. There is currently no API to alter an existing association. It must first be dropped followed by applying the new association. The names of all existing policy expressions can be found in the REDACTION_EXPRESSIONS catalog view. If DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY was invoked, provide an OBJECT_SCHEMA that is not the APEX or Spatial installation schema. Data redaction policies are not supported on objects within the APEX or Spatial installation schema. If DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY was invoked, provide an OBJECT_NAME that does not reference either a metadata-linked view or an OLAP analytic workspace table.
params: 1) parameter_name: The name of the parameter that had an error. 2) parameter_value: The value that had an error.

description: SQL construct not supported by data redaction.
cause: The query had a SQL construct that was not supported by data redaction.
action: Check the Oracle Documentation for the correct syntax, rewrite the query to avoid using an unsupported construct, and retry.

description: The parameter %s is unexpected for ACTION %s for ALTER_POLICY.
cause: The parameter in PL/SQL function was not NULL or was not equal to the default value. If DBMS_REDACT.ALTER_POLICY was invoked, the parameters object_name and policy_name are required. If the action is DBMS_REDACT.ADD_COLUMN or DBMS_REDACT.MODIFY_COLUMN, only the following parameters are accepted: - Required: * column_name * Only when function_type is DBMS_REDACT.PARTIAL * function_parameters * Only when function_type is DBMS_REDACT.REGEXP or DBMS_REDACT.REGEXP_WIDTH * regexp_pattern * regexp_replace_string - Optional: * function_type * policy_description * column_description * Only when function_type is DBMS_REDACT.REGEXP or DBMS_REDACT.REGEXP_WIDTH * regexp_position * regexp_occurrence * regexp_match_parameter If the action is DBMS_REDACT.DROP_COLUMN, it only accepts the required column_name parameter. If the action is DBMS_REDACT.MODIFY_EXPRESSION, it only accepts the following parameters: - Required: * expression - Optional: * policy_description If the action is DBMS_REDACT.SET_POLICY_DESCRIPTION, it only accepts the optional policy_description parameter. If the action is DBMS_REDACT.SET_COLUMN_DESCRIPTION, it only accepts the following parameters: - Required: * column_name - Optional: * column_description Other parameters are not supported.
action: Do not use parameters that are not supported.
params: 1) parameter_name: The parameter name that is unexpected. 2) action: The action chosen for ALTER_POLICY.

description: The parameter %s is unexpected for ADD_POLICY.
cause: The parameter in the call to the PL/SQL procedure was not NULL or was not equal to the default value. If DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY was called, the parameters OBJECT_NAME and POLICY_NAME are required. If no COLUMN_NAME parameter was provided to DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY, then it only accepts the EXPRESSION, OBJECT_SCHEMA, ENABLE, and POLICY_DESCRIPTION parameters. The EXPRESSION parameter is required. The OBJECT_SCHEMA, ENABLE, and POLICY_DESCRIPTION parameters are optional. If a COLUMN_NAME parameter was provided to DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY and the FUNCTION_TYPE parameter was DBMS_REDACT.PARTIAL, then the parameter FUNCTION_PARAMETERS is required and the parameters FUNCTION_TYPE, POLICY_DESCRIPTION, and COLUMN_DESCRIPTION are optional. If a COLUMN_NAME parameter was provided to DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY and the FUNCTION_TYPE parameter was DBMS_REDACT.REGEXP or DBMS_REDACT.REGEXP_WIDTH, then the parameters REGEXP_PATTERN and REGEXP_REPLACE_STRING are required and REGEXP_POSITION, REGEXP_OCCURRENCE, REGEXP_MATCH_PARAMETER, FUNCTION_TYPE, POLICY_DESCRIPTION, and COLUMN_DESCRIPTION are optional.
action: Do not use combinations of parameters that are not supported.
params: 1) parameter_name: The parameter name that is unexpected.

description: A data redaction policy cannot be applied to an object owned by SYS.
cause: An attempt was made to apply a data redaction policy to an object owned by SYS. Redaction policies cannot be applied to SYS-owned objects.
action: Do not apply a redaction policy to any SYS-owned object. You can apply a redaction policy to an object that is not owned by SYS.

description: Profile limits PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME and PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME are not unlimited, password will expire within %s days.
cause: The password of the user's account expired and entered the grace period and should be changed. This can happen if any of the following is true: - The user account is associated with a password profile with a limited PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME and a non-zero PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME. - The user account is created as part of either a database import inside a pluggable database (PDB) or clone of an existing PDB and the user's password does not meet the requirements of the mandatory profile (that is configured with a limited password grace period) enforced in the PDB. Since the password grace period has not yet elapsed, the user is not prompted to input a new password and an ORA-28098 warning message continues to be displayed upon each successful login to the user account, until the user changes their password. After the grace period has elapsed, the password expires and until the user successfully changes their password their login continues to fail with an ORA-28001 error.
action: Change the password or contact the database administrator to understand the rules for choosing a new password that complies with the mandatory profile.

description: Hexadecimal data cannot be redacted.
cause: The column has a data type that is not supported by data redaction. The supported data types are CHAR, NCHAR, VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, NUMBER, BINARY_FLOAT, BINARY_DOUBLE, DATE, TIMESTAMP, CLOB, NCLOB, BLOB, and BOOLEAN.
action: Specify the name of a column that has a supported data type. Use UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_VARCHAR2 and HEXTORAW functions to avoid the error.

description: VPD policy function does not exist.
cause: The schema owning the Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy function did not exist.
action: Drop the VPD policy and re-create it with a policy function owned by a valid user.

description: A VPD or FGA policy already exists for the specified object.
cause: A Virtual Private Database (VPD) or Fine-Grained Auditing (FGA) policy with the same name for the same object already existed. Policy names applied to an object must be unique for VPD or FGA.
action: Check if the policy has already been added or use a different policy name: - If adding a VPD policy, check DBA_POLICIES to see if a policy with the same name exists. - If adding an FGA policy, check DBA_AUDIT_POLICIES to see if a policy with the same name exists.

description: The OLS, VPD or FGA operation failed because the security policy does not exist.
cause: The Oracle Label Security (OLS), Virtual Private Database (VPD), or Fine-Grained Audit (FGA) operation on a non-existent security policy failed.
action: Try the operation on an existing security policy. Check the following database dictionary views to find valid policies for the feature: - OLS: DBA_SA_POLICIES - VPD: DBA_POLICIES - FGA: ALL_AUDIT_POLICIES

description: An Oracle Label Security (OLS) policy cannot be applied to an object owned by SYS.
cause: An attempt was made to apply an OLS policy to an object owned by SYS. OLS policies cannot be applied to SYS-owned objects.
action: Do not apply an OLS policy to any SYS-owned object. You can apply an OLS policy to an object that is not owned by SYS.

description: input value for %s is not valid
cause: Input value for the argument was not valid.
action: Specify a valid argument value.

description: could not create security-relevant column policy on an object view
cause: The security-relevant column argument was not null in the policy creation for an object view.
action: Do not specify a security-relevant column argument during the policy creation for an object view.

description: Input value for argument #%s is invalid.
cause: Input values for the argument were missing or invalid.
action: Correct the input value for the specified argument.
params: 1) argument_number: The argument number whose input is invalid.

description: Oracle Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy is disabled.
cause: An attempt was made to refresh the VPD policy that had been disabled.
action: Ensure that the VPD policy is enabled before refreshing it.

description: Circular Oracle Virtual Private Database (VPD) security policies detected.
cause: VPD security policies for the same object referenced each other which could lead to infinite looping while processing the object.
action: Examine the policy function for the predicate generated by the function. If the predicate references the object on which the policy has been created, then change the predicate because this could lead to infinite looping of applying the policy on the same object.

description: Number of related policies exceeded the maximum allowed limit of 16.
cause: Too many policies were enabled on the same object.
action: Drop or disable one or more policies.

description: The VPD policy function or package "%s.%s" has error.
cause: The Oracle Virtual Private Database (VPD), row-level security, or fine-grained access control policy function was either invalid or may have been dropped.
action: Check the status of the VPD policy function by querying DBA_OBJECTS and correct the problem. If the policy refers to a missing function, then either re-create the function or use a different function.
params: 1) owner: Owner of the function or package. 2) name: Name of the function or package.

description: insufficient privilege to evaluate policy predicate
cause: Predicate has a subquery which contains objects that the owner of policy function does not have privilege to access.
action: Grant appropriate privileges to the policy function owner.

description: failed to execute policy function with oci error "%s".
cause: The policy function encountered one or more errors during execution.
action: Check the trace file and correct the errors.

description: A virtual private database policy (VPD) predicate error has occurred.
cause: A virtual private database (row-level security, fine-grained access control) policy function generated an invalid predicate for a statement.
action: Contact your database administrator. The DBA will need to review the existing VPD policy and trace files for more detailed error information.

description: policy with check option violation
cause: Policy predicate was evaluated to FALSE with the updated values.
action: Check the trace file and correct the errors.

description: insufficient privileges to do direct path access
cause: Users with insufficient privileges attempting to do direct path access of tables with fine grain access control policies.
action: Ask the database administrator to do the operation. Note that users can work with security administrator to temporarily drop/disable the policies at time of export, import, or load, but this has security implication, and thus access of the database must be controlled carefully.

description: integrity constraint violated - parent record not found
cause: try to update/insert a child record with new foreign key values, but the corresponding parent row is not visible because of fine-grained security in the parent.
action: make sure that the updated foreign key values must also visible in the parent

description: The VPD policy group name already exists for the table or view.
cause: An attempt was made to create an Oracle Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy group with a name that already exists for that table or view.
action: Review the list of existing VPD policy groups for an object in DBA_POLICY_GROUPS. Either use the existing VPD policy group if appropriate or create a new VPD policy group name that is unique for the object.

description: policy group does not exist
cause: An attempt was made to drop a policy group that did not exist or an attempt was made to create a policy in a policy group that did not exist.
action: Specify an existing policy group name.

description: driving context already exists
cause: An attempt was made to create a context that already existed in the system.
action: Create the context with a name that is not already in use.

description: The VPD driving context does not exist for the object.
cause: An attempt was made to drop a Virtual Private Database (VPD) driving context that did not exist. Either the driving context was already removed or the parameter values were incorrect.
action: Review the existing VPD driving contexts in the DBA_POLICY_CONTEXTS view for valid parameter values and run the statement again.

description: cannot update SYS_DEFAULT policy group
cause: An attempt was made to execute either DBMS_RLS.CREATE_POLICY_GROUP or DBMS_RLS.DELETE_POLICY_GROUP using SYS_DEFAULT as the policy group name.
action: Do not attempt to CREATE or DELETE the SYS_DEFAULT policy group.

description: Driving context "%s,%s" contains invalid group "%s".
cause: The previous call to the DBMS_SESSION.SET_CONTEXT package specified an invalid policy group.
action: Review the DBA_POLICY_CONTEXTS and DBA_POLICY_GROUPS views to review driving contexts, objects, and policy associations. Ensure that a valid policy group is passed to the DBMS_SESSION.SET_CONTEXT package when initializing a policy driving context.
params: 1) context: The driving context. 2) attribute: The driving attribute. 3) group_name: The invalid group name.

description: Column %s in SEC_RELEVANT_COLS cannot be of an object data type.
cause: A column specified in the SEC_RELEVANT_COLS argument in a DBMS_RLS package procedure was of an object data type that is not allowed.
action: Ensure that none of the columns specified in SEC_RELEVANT_COLS argument is of an object data type or XMLType.

description: A protected base column was referenced in an unprotected virtual column expression.
cause: A protected base column was referenced in an unprotected virtual column expression. Referencing the unprotected virtual column is not allowed because it could disclose data contained in the protected base column.
action: Check the policy definition and ensure that the virtual column is also protected.

description: Attribute association failed for Oracle Virtual Private Database policy "%s".
cause: An attempt was made to associate a global application context attribute to either a context-sensitive or shared context-sensitive policy. Only local application context attribute association is supported.
action: Retry the operation specifying a local application context attribute.
params: 1) policy_name: The name of the row-level security (RLS) policy.

description: DDL statements are not allowed inside the FGA handler
cause: An attempt was made to execute a DDL statement inside the FGA (Fine Grained Audit) handler.
action: Remove the DDL statement from the handler and retry the operation.

description: Fine Grained Access Control enforced
cause: NA
action: NA

description: The MERGE INTO syntax does not support the security policy.
cause: The MERGE INTO syntax did not support a security policy on the destination table, because the policy's statement types did not include INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE or the policy had a security-relevant column.
action: If you do not have the privilege to modify the security policy, then instead of MERGE INTO, use the INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE DML statements on the table with a security policy defined. If you have the privilege to modify the security policy, then redefine the policy so that statement types include all of the DML statement types (INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE) or ensure that the policy does not have a security-relevant column.

description: Full table access is restricted by Oracle Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy.
cause: The command required full table access but the user was not SYS and did not have the privilege to bypass VPD policies.
action: Grant appropriate privileges, or change the policy function so that it returns a NULL predicate under certain session environments.

description: This object cannot have VPD row-level security policy.
cause: An attempt was made to apply a virtual private database (VPD) (row-level security, fine-grained access) policy on an object. Only tables, views, or synonyms of tables or views can have VPD policies.
action: Apply the virtual private database policy only on tables, views, or synonyms.

description: VPD check option silent error event
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Ignore check option error
cause: NA
action: NA

description: invalid schema for the fine-grained auditing (FGA) audit handler
cause: An invalid schema was specified for the audit handler.
action: Specify a valid schema for the audit handler.

description: error in evaluating the fine grained audit policy predicate
cause: An invalid policy predicate was specified for the FGA (Fine Grained Audit) policy.
action: Specify a valid policy Predicate for the FGA (Fine Grained Audit) policy.

description: Maximum allowed fine-grained audit policies exceeded.
cause: A maximum of 256 fine-grained audit policies can be enabled on an object.
action: Drop or disable existing policies before creating more fine-grained audit policies.

description: invalid column specified during fine-grained audit policy creation
cause: An invalid column name was specified during fine-grained audit policy creation.
action: Specify a valid column name. Do not specify an object column.

description: error in creating XML audit index file
cause: The file holding XML audit file names could not be created. This is relevant in traditional audit with AUDIT_TRAIL=XML.
action: Examine the directory pointed to by the initialization parameter AUDIT_FILE_DEST. Ensure that all of the following are true: - The directory exists. - The name points to a directory and not to a file. - The directory is accessible and writable to the Oracle user.

description: error in accessing XML audit index file
cause: The file holding XML audit file names could not be accessed. This is relevant in traditional audit with AUDIT_TRAIL=XML initialization parameter.
action: Ensure that the file exists in the directory pointed to by the AUDIT_FILE_DEST initialization parameter and can be read by the Oracle user.

description: Invalid argument passed to DBMS_FGA.ADD_POLICY procedure.
cause: Invalid input argument was specified for the DBMS_FGA.ADD_POLICY procedure.
action: Specify correct type and number of arguments to the DBMS_FGA.ADD_POLICY procedure.

description: failure to process fine-grained audit handler
cause: An error was encountered while executing fine-grained audit handler.
action: Refer to the trace file for details.

description: XDS policy already exists for %s
cause: An XDS policy was enabled for an object that already has an associated XDS policy.
action: Specify a different policy name or call enable_xds with the overwrite paramter set to TRUE.

description: invalid operation for Oracle Virtual Private Database policy "%s"
cause: Attribute association (NAMESPACE, ATTRIBUTE) was specified for an invalid policy type. Attribute association can be set only for context-sensitive and shared context-sensitive policy types.
action: Use a context-sensitive or shared context-sensitive policy when specifying the attribute association.
params: 1) policy_name: The name of the row-level security (RLS) policy.

description: The specified attribute association ("%s", "%s") is already attached to VPD policy "%s".
cause: An attempt was made to create an attribute association to the existing Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy using namespace and attribute names that were already used by an existing attribute association of the policy.
action: Review the existing set of namespace and attribute associations for the VPD policy in DBA_POLICY_CONTEXTS view, and retry the operation with valid namespace and attribute values.
params: 1) namespace: The name of the namespace. 2) attribute: The name of the attribute. 3) name: The name of the policy.

description: The specified attribute association ("%s", "%s") is not attached to policy "%s".
cause: An attempt was made to drop the attribute association that was not attached to the policy.
action: Review the existing set of namespace and attribute associations for the Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy in the DBA_POLICY_CONTEXTS view, and retry the operation with valid namespace and attribute values.
params: 1) namespace: The name of the namespace. 2) attribute: The name of the attribute. 3) policy_name: The name of the policy.

description: Value for "%s" is either invalid or missing.
cause: The value provided for the NAMESPACE or ATTRIBUTE argument was invalid or missing.
action: Provide a valid value for both NAMESPACE and ATTRIBUTE arguments.
params: 1) policy_argument: The NAMESPACE or ATTRIBUTE argument.

description: The proxy user is not authorized to connect as client.
cause: A proxy user attempted to connect as a client, but the proxy user was not authorized to act on behalf of the client.
action: Grant the proxy user permission to perform actions on behalf of the client by using the ALTER USER ... GRANT CONNECT command.

description: more than one user name specified for command
cause: More than one user name was specified for an ALTER USER command.
action: Try the command again with only one user name.

description: proxy user '%s' may not specify initial role '%s' on behalf of client '%s'
cause: A proxy user attempted to specify an initial role for a client, but the client does not possess the role.
action: Change the proxy user so that it does not specify the role or grant the role to the client.

description: invalid client initial role specified: "%s"
cause: A role specified by a proxy user as an initial role to be activated upon connecting on behalf of a client was invalid.
action: Connect again as the client specifying a valid role.
params: 1) role_name: The name of the role.

description: proxy user may not act as client '%s'
cause: A proxy user attempted to assume the identity of a privileged user in order to limit the privileges that a proxy may possess.
action: Call the statement again specifying a client other than a privileged user.
params: 1) user_name: The proxy client user name.

description: user '%s' specified as a proxy is actually a role
cause: A user specified in an AUDIT <operation> BY <proxy> ON BEHALF OF <client> is actually a role.
action: Execute the statement again with a valid proxy user.

description: Proxy user '%s' not authorized to set role '%s' for client '%s'
cause: A proxy user has not been granted the right to use a role on behalf of a client.
action: Execute the command ALTER USER <client> GRANT CONNECT THROUGH PROXY <proxy> to grant the needed role.

description: Proxy user '%s' forbidden to set role '%s' for client '%s'
cause: A proxy user was forbidden to use a role on behalf of a client through the command ALTER USER <client> GRANT CONNECT THROUGH <proxy> WITH ALL ROLES EXCEPT <role>
action: Execute the command ALTER USER <client> GRANT CONNECT THROUGH PROXY <proxy> to grant the needed role.

description: missing ALL keyword
cause: Keyword missing.
action: Provide missing keyword.

description: missing BEHALF keyword
cause: Keyword missing.
action: Provide missing keyword.

description: missing EXCEPT keyword
cause: Keyword missing.
action: Provide missing keyword.

description: missing ROLES keyword in the statement
cause: The keyword ROLES was not specified in the statement.
action: Check the syntax of the statement and ensure that the keyword ROLES is part of the statement. Then, run the statement again.

description: missing THROUGH keyword
cause: Keyword missing.
action: Provide missing keyword.

description: GRANT already specified
cause: The GRANT clause was specified twice.
action: Use only one GRANT clause.

description: REVOKE already specified
cause: The REVOKE clause was specified twice.
action: Use only one REVOKE clause.

description: proxy '%s' may not specify password-protected role '%s' for client '%s'
cause: A proxy user attempted to activate a role on behalf of a client which has a password associated with it. Since the proxy does not have a password, this activation cannot be allowed.
action: Attempt to activate a different role or change the role administratively so that there is no password.

description: A role has been listed more than once in the Audit Policy statement.
cause: The name of a role has been specified more than once in the Audit Policy statement. Each role must be listed only once.
action: Review the Audit Policy statement, and ensure that each role is listed only once.

description: unused error
cause: NA
action: NA

description: unsupported certificate type
cause: The type of certificate from which the server is to extract the credentials of the client is not supported.
action: Specify a supported type.

description: unsupported certificate version
cause: The version of the certificate from which the server is to extract the credentials of the client is not supported.
action: Specify a supported version.

description: unsupported Kerberos version
cause: the version the Kerberos ticket which the server is to use to validate the identity of the client is not supported.
action: Specify a supported version.

description: Kerberos ticket not provided by proxy
cause: A client user is to be authenticated using a Kerberos ticket but none was provided by the proxy user.
action: Provide a Kerberos ticket.

description: incorrect certificate type
cause: the type of certificate provided by the proxy user to identify a client user does not match the type that is required.
action: Provide a certificate of the correct type.

description: incorrect certificate version
cause: the version of certificate provided by the proxy user to identify a client user does not match the version that is required.
action: Provide a certificate of the correct version.

description: incorrect Kerberos ticket version
cause: the version of Kerberos ticket provided by the proxy user to authenticate a client user does not match the version that is required.
action: Provide a Kerberos ticket of the correct version.

description: client user name not provided by proxy
cause: No user name was provided by the proxy user for the client user.
action: Either specify a client database user name, a distinguished name or an X.509 certificate.

description: multiple authentication methods provided by proxy
cause: More than one authentication method was specified by the proxy user for the client user.
action: Specify only one of the following: a client database user name, a distinguished name or an X.509 certificate.

description: The proxy user "%s" failed to enable one or more of the specified default roles for client user "%s".
cause: One or more default roles specified for the client user were not enabled for the proxy user. Only roles directly granted to the client user, not password protected and not a secure application role, can be enabled as a default role.
action: Review the roles granted to the client user in the DBA_ROLES_PRIVS view. The default role must be directly granted to the client user. Check the DBA_ROLES.AUTHENTICATION_TYPE view for the roles. Only roles with AUTHENTICATION_TYPE=NONE can be default roles. You can do one or more of the following: - Remove the non-compliant role from the list of default roles. - Change the AUTHENTICATION_TYPE for the role. - Enable the role as an application role or password role after login.
params: 1) proxy_user_name: The name of the proxy user. 2) client_user_name: The name of the client user.

description: cannot acquire Kerberos service ticket for client
cause: An attempt to use a Kerberos ticket that can be forwarded to obtain a Kerberos service ticket for the client failed.
action: Ensure that: - The Kerberos ticket required for the Kerberos service ticket is valid. - The key distribution center is available.

description: proper authentication not provided by proxy
cause: A client user must be authenticated but no authentication credentials were provided by the proxy user.
action: Provide the proper authentication credentials.

description: Global user cannot have proxy permissions managed in the directory.
cause: The client name specified was a global user that could not have proxy permissions.
action: Use ALTER USER to change the type of user (from IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY to something else such as IDENTIFIED BY password or IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY) and then grant proxy permissions.

description: cannot change a user with administrative privilege to proxy-only connect user
cause: An attempt was made to alter a user with an administrative privilege to a proxy-only connect user. This is not permitted because proxy users cannot connect to the database with administrative privilege.
action: Remove the PROXY ONLY CONNECT property for the user and retry granting an administrative privilege to the user.

description: cannot grant %s to a proxy-only connect user
cause: An attempt was made to grant an administrative privilege like SYSDBA, SYSOPER, SYSASM, SYSBACKUP, SYSDG, SYSKM, or SYSRAC to a proxy-only connect user. Since proxy authentication using an administrative privilege is not supported, such grants are not allowed.
action: Grant administrative privileges only to accounts that are not marked "proxy only connect".
params: 1) privilege_name: The name of an administrative privilege.

description: cannot alter global user to proxy-only connect user
cause: An attempt was made to alter global user to proxy-only connect.
action: none

description: cannot alter user SYS/SYSBACKUP/SYSDG/SYSKM/SYSRAC to be identified as globally
cause: An attempt was made to alter SYS/SYSBACKUP/SYSDG/SYSKM/SYSRAC to be identified as globally.
action: none

description: SYSRAC administrative privilege cannot be granted to database users.
cause: An attempt was made to grant SYSRAC administrative privilege to a database user. The SYSRAC administrative privilege is used only by the Oracle agent of Oracle Clusterware to connect to the database using operating system authentication.
action: Use connection string '/ as SYSRAC' from an operating system account in the OSRAC group to connect to the database with the SYSRAC privilege.

description: cannot grant administrative privileges to a user with non-ASCII or non-EBCDIC characters in the user name
cause: Attempt to grant an administrative privilege to a user failed. Administrative privileges like SYSDBA, SYSOPER, SYSASM, SYSBACKUP, SYSDG, and SYSKM cannot be granted to a user with non-ASCII or non-EBCDIC characters in the user name.
action: Grant administrative privileges to a user whose name contains ASCII or EBCDIC characters only.

description: Enabling or disabling read-only property is not allowed on a common user.
cause: An attempt was made to enable or disable the read-only property on a common user. Only local users can be set to read-only.
action: Do not attempt to enable or disable the read-only property on a common user.

description: Can perform read operations only
cause: Session is marked read only
action: Unset read_only parameter for the session

description: Can perform read operations only
cause: User is marked read only
action: Please contact your database administrator

description: cannot enable hybrid read only mode when pluggable database is open in upgrade mode
cause: An attempt was made to enable hybrid read only mode when pluggable database was opened in upgrade mode.
action: Open the pluggable database in read write mode to set the hybrid read only mode.

description: IDENTIFIED USING already specified
cause: The IDENTIFIED USING clause was specified twice.
action: Use only one IDENTIFIED USING clause.

description: An invalid command was used to enable secure application role "%s".
cause: An attempt was made to enable the secure application role without using the designated package that enables the role. Secure application roles can only be enabled by executing the package that secures the role.
action: Enable the secure application role by executing the designated package for the role.
params: 1) role_name: The name of the secure role.

description: password length less than %d characters
cause: The password entered by the user did not meet the minimum length criteria.
action: Enter a password which meets the minimum length criteria.

description: password contains the user name
cause: The provided password contained the user name.
action: Enter a password that does not contain the user name.

description: password contains the user name in reverse
cause: The provided password contained the reverse of the user name.
action: Enter a password that does not contain the reverse of the user name.

description: password contains the server name
cause: The provided password contained the server name.
action: Enter a password that does not contain the server name.

description: password too simple
cause: The password was simple enough to guess.
action: Enter a complex paswword.

description: new password should differ from the old password by %s or more characters
cause: The new and old passwords should differ by at least the minimum number of characters as defined by the administrator.
action: Enter a password that differs from the previous password by at least the minimum required number of changed characters, as defined by the administrator.

description: password must NOT contain a double-quotation
cause: The double-quotation mark character is reserved as a password delimiter.
action: Enter a password without any double-quotation marks.

description: password must contain %d or more letters
cause: The password did not meet the minimum required number of alphabetic characters.
action: Enter a password containing at least the minimum number of alphabetic characters.

description: password must contain %d or more uppercase characters
cause: The password did not meet the minimum required number of uppercase alphabetic characters.
action: Enter a password containing at least the minimum number of uppercase alphabetic characters.

description: password must contain %d or more lowercase characters
cause: The password did not meet the minimum required number lowercase alphabetic characters.
action: Enter a password containing at least the minimum number of lowercase alphabetic characters.

description: password must contain %d or more digits
cause: The password did not contain the minimum number of digits.
action: Enter a password comtaining at least the minimum number of digits.

description: password must contain %d or more special characters
cause: The password did not contain the minimum number of special characters.
action: Enter a password containing at least the minimum number of special characters.

description: password length more than 1024 bytes
cause: The length of the password exceeded 1024 bytes.
action: Enter a password containing a maximum of 1024 bytes.

description: password verification failed for mandatory profile
cause: The new password did not meet the necessary password complexity requirements defined by the mandatory profile.
action: Contact your system administrator for the rules about choosing the new password.

description: invalid schema name %s or password verification function %s
cause: A nonexistent or invalid schema name or password verification function was specified. This occurred when you attempted to create or alter a profile with PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION parameter value containing a non-SYS user owned schema qualified function and either of the following was true: - The ALLOWED_PVF_OWNERS system parameter was not configured to allow schema qualified password verification function. - The user schema was not allowed to own the password verification function. - The password verification function was created as an INVOKER rights PL/SQL function.
action: Specify a valid schema name or password verification function for PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION parameter. Depending on the error, either one of the following should be done: - If the ALLOWED_PVF_OWNERS system parameter is set to NULL (default value), please contact your database administrator to have it set it to an appropriate value (comma separated list of database users) to allow schema qualified password verification function. - If the user schema is not allowed to own the password verification function, please contact your database administrator to add the user as part of ALLOWED_PVF_OWNERS system parameter value. Only users specified as ALLOWED_PVF_OWNERS system parameter value are allowed to own password verification function. - If the password verification function is created as an INVOKER rights PL/SQL function, please create it as DEFINER rights PL/SQL function and retry {CREATE|ALTER} PROFILE operation. INVOKER rights PL/SQL functions are not allowed as password verification function due to security reasons.

description: REPLACE clause not specified
cause: An attempt was made to change the password with the password verification function enabled and the original password was not specified in the REPLACE clause. This is required if the user does not have ALTER USER system privilege.
action: Provide the original password in the REPLACE clause and retry the operation.

description: Operations cannot be performed on Oracle reserved user or role "%s".
cause: An attempt was made to either change the Oracle reserved user or role, or grant a role or privilege to the Oracle reserved user or role. Operations are not allowed on this Oracle reserved user or role.
action: Do not perform this operation on the Oracle reserved user or role.

description: first login requires password change
cause: This user was globally authenticated. Password policy settings in Oracle Internet Directory (OID) requires the password to be changed for the first connection. Further connections to the database will be denied if the password in OID is not changed.
action: Connect to the OID to change the password.

description: user password or account management tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support or development.
action: None.

description: The EXPIRE PASSWORD ROLLOVER PERIOD clause is specified with a disallowed IDENTIFIED clause or a NO AUTHENTICATION clause
cause: The ALTER USER statement incorrectly included a disallowed IDENTIFIED clause or a NO AUTHENTICATION clause with the EXPIRE PASSWORD ROLLOVER PERIOD clause.
action: Use only one of the above clauses in the ALTER USER statement and resubmit the command.

description: EXPIRE PASSWORD ROLLOVER PERIOD clause already specified
cause: In ALTER USER statement the EXPIRE PASSWORD ROLLOVER PERIOD clause was specified more than once.
action: Remove all but one of the EXPIRE PASSWORD ROLLOVER PERIOD clauses and resubmit the command.

description: Gradual password rollover is not supported for application users with administrative privilege.
cause: An attempt is being made to grant an administrative privilege to an application user that is associated with a password profile having a non-zero value for the PASSWORD_ROLLOVER_TIME profile limit. The gradual password rollover feature is not supported for application users with administrative privilege.
action: Ensure that the application user being granted the administrative privilege is not associated with a password profile having a non-zero PASSWORD_ROLLOVER_TIME limit, and retry the operation.

description: REPLACE clause not specified when the password was being changed.
cause: An attempt was made to change the password of a user who had been granted one or more administrative privileges. A user with an administrative privilege (SYSOPER, SYSBACKUP...) must supply both the existing and new passwords.
action: Provide the original password using the REPLACE clause. ALTER USER <user> IDENTIFIED BY <new> REPLACE <old>; If you don't know your old password anymore, contact your user or security administrator.

description: The password verification function "%s" was not found or did not have enough privileges.
cause: A nonexistent or invalid function name was specified as the password verification function. This occurrs when either of the following was true: - The current user executing the {CREATE|ALTER} PROFILE DDL did not have EXECUTE privilege granted on the password verification function. - The password verification function was either created as an invalid function or it was invalidated due to dependencies on other database objects.
action: Use a valid function name. Depending on the error, either one of the following should be done: - If you need EXECUTE privilege on the password verification function, contact your database administrator to have the privilege granted. - If the password verification function is in an INVALID state, check the DBA_ERRORS and DBA_OBJECTS view for more information.
params: 1) function_name: The name of the function that could not be executed.

description: no data passed to obfuscation toolkit
cause: A NULL value was passed to a function or procedure.
action: Make sure that the data passed is not empty.

description: invalid input length for obfuscation toolkit
cause: Length of data submitted for encryption or decryption is not a multiple of 8 bytes.
action: Make sure that the length of the data to be encrypted or decrypted is a multiple of 8 bytes.

description: double encryption not supported
cause: The obfuscation toolkit did not support the encryption of already-encrypted data.
action: Do not attempt to encrypt already-encrypted data.

description: invalid key length
cause: The specified key length is invalid for the algorithm. DES requires a key of at least 8 bytes. Triple DES requires a key of least 16 bytes in two-key mode and 24 bytes in three-key mode. AES keys must be exactly 16 bytes long for AES128, 24 bytes long for AES192,and 32 bytes long for AES256.
action: Specify a key of valid length.

description: algorithm not available
cause: The encryption algorithm desired is not available.
action: Run the installer to install the needed algorithm in Oracle Advanced Security.

description: invalid Triple DES mode
cause: An unknown value was specified for the mode in which triple DES encryption is to run.
action: Specify a valid value. See the package declaration for a list of valid values.

description: seed length too short
cause: The seed specified for the key generation routine must be at least 80 characters.
action: Specify a longer seed.

description: no seed provided
cause: A NULL value was passed in as the seed to be used in generating a key.
action: Provide a non-NULL value for the seed.

description: A NULL value was used for the encryption or decryption key.
cause: A NULL value was passed in as an encryption or decryption key.
action: Provide a non-NULL value for the key.

description: CURRENT_USER can not be used in PLSQL Definer's Right procedure.
cause: An attempt to retrieve CURRENT_USER using SYS_CONTEXT PLSQL interface.
action: Use a SQL statement to query CURRENT_USER inside a DR procedure.

description: Global application context cannot be used after failing over with Transparent Application Continuity.
cause: An attempt was made to retrieve the global application context value in a failed-over session.
action: Determine if the application can use Application Continuity instead of Transparent Application Continuity, or use the local application context instead of the global application context.

description: unused error
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Client identifier is too long.
cause: The length of the client identifier was longer than 64 bytes.
action: Set a client identifier with a length less than or equal to 64 bytes.

description: Namespace beginning with 'SYS_' is not allowed.
cause: Namespace beginning with 'SYS_' was not allowed.
action: Use a namespace that does not begin with 'SYS_'.

description: Application Context tracing event
cause: N/A
action: THIS IS NOT A USER ERROR NUMBER/MESSAGE. THIS DOES NOT NEED TO BE TRANSLATED OR DOCUMENTED. IT IS USED ONLY FOR DEBUGGING.

description: An invalid value was provided for the context namespace.
cause: Either the value of the context namespace conflicts with reserved keywords or a secure namespace was not allowed for this type of application context.
action: Specify a valid value for the context namespace.

description: Exceeded maximum number of entries for context information in a session.
cause: The number of entries in the current session context exceeded 10,000 which is the maximum number allowed for a session.
action: Review session context entries in the SESSION_CONTEXT view and clear unwanted context entries before setting new context entries.

description: Event to enable overwrite of client_identifier when client_info is set
cause: N/A
action: Set this event in your environment to propagate client_info session context attribute to client_identifier.
note: THIS IS NOT A USER ERROR NUMBER/MESSAGE. THIS DOES NOT NEED TO BE TRANSLATED OR DOCUMENTED.

description: Malformed user nickname for password authenticated global user.
cause: An attempt to login as password-auuthenticated global user with a malformed user nickname.
action: Make sure the nickname is valid and re-login.

description: No permission to read user entry in LDAP directory service.
cause: ORACLE server does not have read permission on user nickname's X.500 user entry.
action: Make sure ORACLE server is using right SSL credentials to connect to LDAP directory services. Make sure permissions for LDAP user entries are right.

description: Domain policy restricts password based GLOBAL user authentication.
cause: Domain policy does not allow password-authenticated GLOBAL users.
action: Make sure ORACLE server is using right SSL credentials to connect to LDAP directory services. Make sure orclDBAuthTypes attributes within Oracle enterprise domain object is either set to PWD or ALL.

description: No mapping for user nickname to LDAP distinguished name exists.
cause: ORACLE server cannot map the given user nickname to LDAP distinguished name.
action: Make sure user entries in LDAP are correctly provisioned with correct user nickname attribute values.

description: No ORACLE password attribute corresponding to user nickname exists.
cause: LDAP user entry corresponding to user nickname does not have a ORACLE password attribute or the attribute is not initialized.
action: Make sure user entries in LDAP are correctly provisioned with correct ORACLE password attribute values.

description: Multiple mappings for user nickname to LDAP distinguished name exist.
cause: The given user nickname maps to more than one LDAP distinguished name.
action: Make sure user nickname is unique within the enterprise.

description: Invalid ORACLE password attribute.
cause: The ORACLE password attribute of a user entry has an invalid format.
action: Make sure ORACLE password attribute value is RFC-2307 compliant.

description: LDAP search, while authenticating global user with passwords, failed.
cause: The LDAP search for finding the appropriate user entry and ORACLE password failed.
action: Make sure LDAP directory service is up and running.

description: No domain policy registered for password based GLOBAL users.
cause: No policy about password authenticated GLOBAL users has been registered.
action: Add attribute orclDBAuthTypes to the database server's Enterprise domain.

description: Error reading ldap_directory_access init parameter.
cause: ldap_directory_access parameter is not specified corrrectly.
action: Make sure spfile.ora has ldap_directory_access set correctly. Possible correct values are PASSWORD, SSL and NONE.

description: Multiple entries for ORACLE database password exist.
cause: The ORACLE password attribute of a user entry has multiple entries of ORACLE database password.
action: Make sure ORACLE password attribute has one entry for ORACLE Database password.

description: Global application context is not updated on one or more Oracle RAC instances.
cause: There was a failure while propagating the global application context values across Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) instances. The background process may have hit an error or the request timed out.
action: Ensure every Oracle RAC instance is operational and retry the operation.

description: Multiple entries found for the same Kerberos Principal Name
cause: Multiple user entries has been configured with the same krbPrincipalName
action: Modify enterprise user's entry to assign its Kerberos principal name Make sure the user entries in LDAP are provisioned correctly.

description: No Kerberos Principal Value found.
cause: Oracle server fails to get value of krbPrincipalName attribute
action: Make sure user entries are correctly provisioned with correct Kerberos principal value

description: No Domain Policy registered for Kerberos based authentication
cause: The enterprise domain entry is not configured for Kerberos based global authentication.
action: Modify orclDBAuthType of the database server's enterprise domain entry and assign it "ALL" or "KRB5"

description: No matched Kerberos Principal found in any user entry
cause: Oracle server fails to find the principal in the user search base
action: Make sure the user search base is correct. Use ESM to configure the enterprise user its Kerberos principal name

description: No permission to read user entry in LDAP directory service.
cause: ORACLE server does not have read permission on user entries.
action: Make sure ORACLE server is using right credentials to connect to LDAP directory services. Make sure permissions for LDAP user entries are configured correctly.

description: Domain Policy hasn't been registered for SSL authentication.
cause: An attempt was made to authenticate with SSL, but the database enterprise domain was not configured for SSL authentication.
action: Modify orclDBAuthType of the server's enterprise domain entry and assign it "ALL" or "SSL".

description: User does not exist in the LDAP directory service.
cause: An attempt was made to authenticate with SSL using the user's certificate, but there was no user entry in the LDAP server that matched the user's Distinguished Name.
action: Add an user entry whose DN matches the user's PKI DN in the LDAP directory.

description: Distinguished name for user exceeds maximum supported length.
cause: The user's distinguished name exceeded the maximum supported length. The maximum allowed length for a distinguished name is 1023 bytes.
action: Create global users with a distinguished name that is less than or equal to 1023 bytes.

description: Oracle encrypted block is corrupt (file # %s, block # %s)
cause: The indicated encrypted block was corrupt. This was an in-memory corruption. The exact cause is unknown. Possible causes could be: - the encryption wallet is incorrect or corrupted - the tablespace encryption key is incorrect or corrupted - decryption engine failure - actual logical error exists in decrypted block
action: Review the encryption wallet and the keys stored in it to ensure they are valid and correct.

description: unable to get valid WALLET_LOCATION
cause: An invalid WALLET_LOCATION was specified in the sqlnet.ora file, or the ORACLE_BASE or ORACLE_HOME environment vairable was not set properly.
action: Correct WALLET_LOCATION in the sqlnet.ora file, or properly set the ORACLE_BASE or ORACLE_HOME environment variable.

description: The directory user has %s groups mapped to different database global users.
cause: A directory user connected to the database while there were multiple directory user groups mapped to different shared database global users (shared schemas).
action: No action is required if, by design, the user's multiple groups need to be mapped to different database global users. However, the database will only pick one global schema for the directory user to map to during login. If only one database global schema mapping is desired, then either create an exclusive database global user mapping for the directory user, or ensure that the directory user has only one mapped shared database global user.

description: The directory current time %s is not valid.
cause: Either the directory service time was earlier than the year 1900, or the format was incorrect.
action: Ensure that the directory service clock is set properly.
params: 1) timestamp: The current time in the directory.

description: The directory server type %s is not supported.
cause: The database tried to work with a directory service which was not supported.
action: Update the dsi.ora or ldap.ora file to reflect an appropriate directory server type.

description: failed to get the service user's credential from the wallet.
cause: An attempt was made to get the service user's credential from the wallet. However, either the wallet was not found or the service user's credential was missing in the wallet.
action: Check the wallet path and update the wallet with the service user's credential.

description: An external or global role with the same external name already exists.
cause: The external name (a distinguished name) specified for the external or global role being created or altered is already mapped to another role.
action: External names must be unique among roles. Review existing roles and associated external names in the DBA_ROLES view. Specify a different external name for the role or use the existing role instead.

description: Oracle encrypted data block not encrypted (file # %s, block # %s)
cause: The indicated data block was found unencrypted in a fully encrypted tablespace. The exact cause is unknown. Possible causes could be: - An encrypted data block is tampered and replaced with an unencrypted data block. - An Oracle internal issue.
action: Collect block dump and redo dump for this block, and contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Proxy user is not supported with DSI.
cause: Proxy user authentication is currently not supported with Directory Service Integration (DSI).
action: Do not use proxy user authentication with DSI.

description: LDAP server connection is down.
cause: The LDAP server is down or the connection to the LDAP server is closed.
action: Retry the connect operation.

description: The current user database link is not supported with DSI.
cause: An attempt was made to use the current user database link with Directory Services Integration (DSI).
action: Do not use the current user database link with DSI.

description: encryption key mismatched for file # %s
cause: Oracle tablespace encryption could not verify the master key or the tablespace key for this data file. The exact cause is unknown. Possible cause could be: - The encryption wallet was incorrect. - The encryption wallet was incorrectly shared between databases. - The tablespace encryption key was incorrect or corrupted.
action: Review the encryption wallet and the keys stored in it to ensure that they are valid, and contact Oracle Support Services.

description: LDAP user, group or domain is not found.
cause: The user, group or domain was not found on the LDAP server.
action: Check the LDAP user name or domain name.

description: The encryption is not allowed for this data type or the data type is invalid.
cause: The data type was not supported for column encryption or the data type was invalid.
action: Use a correct data type.

description: encrypted column size too long for the data type
cause: The column was both encrypted and one of the following: - For VARCHAR2 when extended character data types were disabled, the length specified was greater than 3932. - For VARCHAR2 when extended character data types were enabled, the length specified was greater than 32699. - For CHAR, the length specified was greater than 1932. - For NVARCHAR2 when extended character data types were disabled, the length specified was greater than 1966. - For NVARCHAR2 when extended character data types were enabled, the length specified was greater than 16349. - For NCHAR, the length specified was greater than 966. - For RAW when extended character data types were disabled, the length specified was greater than 3932. - For RAW when extended character data types were enabled, the length specified was greater than 32699.
action: Reduce the column size, or use TDE tablespace encryption.

description: Cannot have more than one password for the encryption key.
cause: More than one password was specified in the command.
action: Revise the command to supply a single password and retry.

description: The column is not encrypted.
cause: An attempt was made to rekey or decrypt an unencrypted column.
action: NA

description: The column is already encrypted.
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a column that is already encrypted.
action: Do not attempt to encrypt a column that is already encrypted.

description: referenced or referencing FK constraint column cannot be encrypted
cause: encrypted columns were involved in the referential constraint
action: NA

description: cannot encrypt SYS owned objects
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt columns in a table that were owned by SYS.
action: Do not attempt to encrypt columns in a table that are owned by SYS or consider using tablespace encryption.

description: the specified index may not be defined on an encrypted column
cause: The index column was a functional, domain, or join index.
action: Do not create a functional, domain, or join index on an encrypted column, or encrypt a column that is already a part of a functional, domain, or join index.

description: Columns cannot be both indexed and encrypted with salt.
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt an index column with salt or an attempt was made to create an index on an encrypted column with salt.
action: Alter the table and specify column encrypting without salt.

description: Missing or invalid encryption algorithm - %s
cause: The specified encryption algorithm was either missing or invalid in the command.
action: Specify a valid algorithm. Refer to the Oracle Database documentation for the list of supported algorithms.
params: 1) algorithm_name: The name of the algorithm.

description: A different encryption algorithm has been chosen for the table or tablespace.
cause: Existing encrypted columns or tablespace were associated with a different algorithm.
action: Do not specify an algorithm, or specify the same one for the existing encrypted columns or tablespace.

description: cannot encrypt constraint columns with salt
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt the constraint columns with salt.
action: Encrypt the constraint columns without salt.

description: integrity check failures on column key
cause: Encryption metadata may have been improperly altered.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: failure to encrypt data or redo
cause: Data or encryption metadata might have been improperly altered or the security module might not have been properly set up: - For redo, a key change might have been in progress or might have been in an invalid key state. - For redo transport, other attempts will be attempted. See the trace files for additional information.
action: For redo, if the problem persists, remove the ENCRYPTION attribute from the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter.

description: fails to decrypt data
cause: Either the data or encryption metadata was improperly altered, or the security module was not properly set up.
action: None.

description: cannot downgrade because there exists encrypted column
cause: An attempt was made to downgrade when there was an encrypted column in the system.
action: Decrypt these columns before attempting to downgrade.

description: An encrypted column cannot serve as a partitioning column.
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a partitioning key column or to create a partitioning index with encrypted columns.
action: Do not encrypt a partitioning key column or decrypt the column before creating the partitioning index.

description: encryption properties mismatch
cause: An attempt was made to issue an ALTER TABLE EXCHANGE PARTITION | SUBPARTITION command, but encryption properties were mismatched.
action: Make sure encryption algorithms and columns keys are identical. The corresponding columns must be encrypted on both tables with the same salt and non-salt flavor.

description: The index that was defined on the specified column cannot be encrypted.
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a column which is in a functional index, domain index, or join index.
action: Drop the index.

description: cannot encrypt the specified column recorded in the materialized view log
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a column which is already recorded in the materialized view log.
action: drop the materialized view log

description: cannot encrypt the specified column recorded in CDC synchronized change table
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a column which is already recorded in CDC synchronized change table.
action: drop the synchronized change table

description: cannot encrypt the column of a cluster key
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a column of the cluster key. A column of the cluster key in a clustered table could not be encrypted.
action: None.

description: event to force ZT error in kzekm
cause: N/A
action: Set this event in your environment to simulate a ZT error.
note: THIS IS NOT A USER ERROR NUMBER/MESSAGE. THIS DOES NOT NEED TO BE TRANSLATED OR DOCUMENTED.

description: Failed to open wallet.
cause: The database is unable to open the security module wallet due to an incorrect wallet path or password. It is also possible that a wallet has not been created. Ensure that the TDE_CONFIGURATION is set to "OKV|FILE" if an external keystore (OKV/KMS) is being used. If the database is configured to use external keystore (OKV/KMS) as the TDE keystore, the database may be having difficulty finding the external configuration file of the keystore.
action: Execute the command again using the correct wallet password or verify that a wallet exists in the specified directory. If necessary, create a new wallet and initialize it. When using external keystore (OKV/KMS), check if the configuration file is in the right directory. When the instance initialization parameter WALLET_ROOT is configured, the Oracle Key Vault configuration file should be located at one of the following paths: $WALLET_ROOT/okv/conf (for CDB$ROOT and united PDBs) $WALLET_ROOT/PDB-GUID/okv/conf (for an isolated PDB) The pluggable database (PDB) GUID can be obtained by querying GUID from the DBA_PDBS view. Also in the case of an external keystore, refer to the documentation for information on endpoint enrollment and provisioning.

description: Encryption wallet, auto login wallet, or HSM is already open.
cause: Either the encryption wallet, auto-login wallet, or the external keystore (OKV/KMS) is already open.
action: The auto-login keystore opens automatically and from the WALLET_TYPE field of V$ENCRYPTION_WALLET check if the auto-login keystore is currently open. ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT SET KEYSTORE CLOSE can be used to close the auto-login keystore.

description: failed to initialize security module
cause: An attempt to perform the cryptographic library operation failed or an invalid operation is being attempted.
action: Check the trace file for more details and contact Oracle Support.

description: invalid open wallet syntax
cause: The command to open the wallet contained improper spelling or syntax.
action: If attempting to open the wallet, verify the spelling and syntax and execute the command again.

description: password required to open the wallet
cause: A password was not provided when executing the open wallet command, the isolate keystore command, or the unite keystore command.
action: Retry the command with a valid password.

description: improper set key syntax
cause: The command to set the master key contained improper spelling or syntax.
action: If attempting to set the master key for Transparent Database Encryption, verify the spelling and syntax and execute the command again.

description: invalid certificate identifier
cause: The certificate that was specified did not exist in the wallet.
action: Query the V$WALLET fixed view to find the proper certificate identifier for certificate to be used.

description: security module internal error
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Master key not yet set.
cause: The master key for the instance is not set.
action: Execute the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT SET KEY command to set a master key for the database instance. If the wallet or the keys were moved to the current database, ensure that the required keys and the mapping for the current key are present. Check the database property in PROPS$ for TDE_MASTER_KEY_ID to list the current key ID.

description: master key not found
cause: The required master key could not be located. This may be caused by the use of an invalid or incorrect wallet.
action: Check the wallet location parameters to see if the correct wallet is specified. Also, verify that a single sign-on (SSO) wallet is not being used when an encrypted wallet is intended.

description: buffer provided not large enough for output
cause: The provided output buffer was too small to contain the output.
action: Check the size of the output buffer to ensure that it is initialized to the proper size.

description: invalid wallet operation
cause: The command to operate the wallet contained improper spelling or syntax.
action: Verify the spelling and syntax and execute the command again.

description: Wallet is not open.
cause: The keystore (FILE wallet or OKV/KMS) is not open.
action: Open the keystore using the keystore password or EXTERNAL STORE. If using auto-login keystore, ensure that the auto-login keystore is present in the correct wallet location depending upon the WALLET_ROOT configuration. Do not use a local auto-login keystore in Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC). If an environment variable is used for the keystore location, ensure that it is set for srvctl and the operating system session. Ensure that the TDE_CONFIGURATION is set to "OKV|FILE" if an external keystore (OKV/KMS) is being used.

description: invalid database encryption operation
cause: The command for database encryption contained improper spelling or syntax.
action: Verify the spelling and syntax and execute the command again.

description: wallet does not exist
cause: The Oracle wallet was not created or the initialization parameter, WALLET_ROOT, specifies an invalid wallet path.
action: Verify that the initialization parameter, WALLET_ROOT, is correct and that a valid wallet exists in the specified path. In case of an external (OKV/KMS) keystore, verify that the external keystore is reachable.

description: cannot auto-create wallet
cause: The database failed to auto create an Oracle wallet. The Oracle process may not have proper file permissions or a wallet may already exist.
action: Confirm that proper directory permissions are granted to the Oracle user and that neither an encrypted or obfuscated wallet exists in the specified wallet location and try again.

description: cannot add files to encryption-ready tablespace when offline
cause: You attempted to add files to an encryption-ready tablespace when all the files in the tablespace were offline.
action: Bring the tablespace online and try again

description: The currently specified encryption option is not allowed on the target tablespace - %s
cause: An attempt is being made to specify one encryption option out of the ENCRYPT, DECRYPT or REKEY on a tablespace, but the target tablespace does not support application of the specified encryption option.
action: Check the error message against the target tablespace property. Re-evaluate whether the currently specified encryption option still applies. Remove this option and retry the statement with a different and suitable option.

description: ENCRYPTION clause or ENCRYPT option not allowed
cause: An attempt was made to specify the ENCRYPTION clause or ENCRYPT option for system and undo tablespaces.
action: Remove one or both of these options and retry the statement.

description: missing ENCRYPT option for encrypted tablespace
cause: An attempt was made to specify the ENCRYPTION property for the CREATE TABLESPACE statement without specifying the ENCRYPT option to encrypt the tablespace.
action: Add the ENCRYPT option and retry the statement.

description: missing or out of order ENCRYPTION clause
cause: An attempt was made to specify the ENCRYPT or DECRYPT option in the CREATE TABLESPACE statement or to specify the ENCRYPT or REKEY option in the ALTER TABLESPACE statement without first specifying the ENCRYPTION property for the tablespace.
action: Add the ENCRYPTION clause or correct the syntax, and retry the statement.

description: typed master key not found in wallet
cause: An attempt is being made to access an encrypted tablespace or redo logs with a typed master key that does not exist in the wallet.
action: Copy the correct Oracle Wallet from the instance where the tablespace was created. Close and open the keystore if the keystore was already open on the database where the keystore was copied. For a PDB unplug/plug or clone operation, verify that the keys were correcly exported and imported by listing the wallet contents using mkstore or orapki. Ensure that the TDE_CONFIGURATION is set to "OKV|FILE" if an external keystore (OKV/KMS) is being used.

description: cross-endian backup conversion of encrypted tablespace is not supported
cause: You attempted to perform a cross-endian backup conversion for encrypted tablespaces.
action: Do not attempt to perform a cross-endian backup conversion of encrypted tablespaces because it is not supported.

description: Cannot find Public-Key Cryptographic Standards #11 (PKCS11) library.
cause: The external keystore (OKV/KMS) vendor PKCS11 library was not found.
action: Place the external keystore (OKV/KMS) vendor library in the following directory structure: For Unix-like systems: /opt/oracle/extapi/[32,64]/hsm/{VENDOR}/{VERSION}/ lib<apiname>.<ext> For Windows systems: %SYSTEM_DRIVE%\oracle\extapi\[32,64]\hsm\{VENDOR}\{VERSION}\ lib<apiname>.<ext> Where: [32, 64] - refers to 32bit or 64bit binary. {VENDOR} - The name of the vendor supplying the library. {VERSION} - Version of the library, preferably in number.number.number format.

description: no need to migrate from FILE wallet to external keystore (OKV/KMS)
cause: The external keystore (OKV/KMS) was already the primary keystore that had the current Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) master key.
action: No action required.

description: Wallet is not opened after setting the master key.
cause: The master key has been set or reset. The wallet needs to be reopened.
action: Reopen the wallet.

description: A different integrity algorithm was used for the column.
cause: The encrypted columns are associated with a different integrity algorithm.
action: Either do not specify an algorithm, or specify the same algorithm used for the existing encrypted columns. The INTALG field of enc$ table provides the current algorithm used by the column.

description: Event to force all newly created tablespaces to be encrypted for testing
cause: N/A
action: Set this event in your environment to force all newly created tablespaces to be encrypted tablespaces. It is an easy way to convert an existing test to run with tablespace encryption. It is used for testing only and not for security. Often run with event 28381.
note: THIS IS NOT A USER ERROR NUMBER/MESSAGE. THIS DOES NOT NEED TO BE TRANSLATED OR DOCUMENTED.

description: event to bypass wallet setup for tablespace encryption
cause: N/A
action: Set this event in your environment to bypass wallet setup for tablespace encryption. It uses a dummy encryption master encryption key to simulate encryption or decryption by the wallet, and has no wallet dependency. This is an easy way to convert an existing test to run with tablespace encryption. It is used for testing only and not for security. Often run with event 28380.
note: THIS IS NOT A USER ERROR NUMBER/MESSAGE. THIS DOES NOT NEED TO BE TRANSLATED OR DOCUMENTED.

description: Global wallet operation in Oracle Real Application Clusters (RAC) failed.
cause: The global wallet operation in RAC failed.
action: For an operation to open or close the wallet, check gv$encryption_wallet view to verify if the wallet operation failed on any instance and retry the operation on the instance where it failed. For an operation to set a new key or secret, check the gv$encryption_keys and gv$client_secrets views to verify if the new secret is correctly shown for all instances. Reopen the wallet on the instances where the new secrets are not correctly listed.

description: Cannot execute a public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate-based master key migration.
cause: A PKI certificate-based master key migration is not allowed.
action: Execute a symmetric master key migration.

description: cannot perform tablespace encryption
cause: Tablespace encryption was attempted when the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate-based primary key was in use.
action: Perform a rekey operation to change to a symmetric Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) master encryption key.

description: cannot perform a PKI certificate-based migration
cause: A PKI certificate-based migration to HSM was attempted.
action: Perform a symmetric Master Key migration.

description: cannot perform a PKI certificate-based master encryption key rekey operation
cause: A public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate-based master encryption key rekey operation was attempted.
action: Perform a symmetric master encryption key rekey operation.

description: could not acquire an enqueue for wallet operation in Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC)
cause: Enqueue to block TDE operations in the Oracle RAC database could not be obtained.
action: Retry the wallet operation.
